messages.subject: Climate data
messages.body_plain:
Hi

May you help me on this. I want to find out about the period covered by the climate data we are using. For example, current data is the average for which period ? And the 2050 and 2070 data is average data for which period?
Regards
Mark
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: Climate data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

               If you're using worldclim data, the current data is averaged for 1970-2000. For future climate data, those are 20-year period monthly averages.

Regards,
Mohammed.

messages.subject: Location of temporary files
messages.body_plain:

 I'm using Wallace 1.9 on a shared windows machine. Each user has limited space. I tried to do projections on different circulation models CCSM and MIROC for Holocene and LGM, but at some point Wallace crashed due to lack of disk space.

 I was wondering, where does Wallace store  temporary files?  Is it possible to delete these environmental files and keep Wallace running?

thanks,

Eric,

messages.subject: Re: Error in v1.9
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jimena,

Again thank you so much for finding this problem. We have fixed it in Wallace 1.9 and you should be able to run your model without problems.

Best,

Andrea

Andrea Paz
PhD candidate
Biology program, Graduate Center
City University of New York

> > Thank you for sending your dataset. I played with it a little and found the source of the issue with the jackknife partition method . I am contacting the ENMeval dev team so we can all work on a solution.
> > In the meantime what seems to be happening is some of your observations are falling within the same cell and are not deleted pre-partitioning so a quick workaround while the code is fixed is for you to thin your dataset before partitioning so that they don’t fall in the same cell. I did this for worldclim 10 min thinning at 20 km and you dataset is left with 59 points and the algorithm works fine. If using ecoclim since the resolution is 0.5 degrees you would have to thin further than that probably around 50 km. Another workaround is for you to delete the localities that are in the same cell before inputting them into Wallace. I hope this fixes you issue for now and I’ll be sure to let you know when an ENMeval or Wallace fix is available so you can update the package.
